title: My Mom Said My Games Would Wreck My Eyes #shorts

cast.kid: a stick-figure boy with a round white head, dot eyes, thin black limbs, short brown hair and an orange hoodie
cast.mom: a stick-figure mother with a round white head, dot eyes, thin black limbs, a curly black ponytail and a purple sweater
cast.grandma: a stick-figure grandmother with a round white head, dot eyes, thin black limbs, a gray bun, round glasses and a green cardigan
cast.doctor: a stick-figure eye doctor with a round white head, dot eyes, thin black limbs, short red hair and a white coat

lines.text: Mom said sitting close to my games would wreck my eyes, so was she right?
lines.image: {kid} sitting on a beanbag right in front of a glowing TV, nose almost touching it, holding a game controller

lines.text: Every night Mom dragged my beanbag back, and every night I scooted it closer again.
lines.image: {mom} alone dragging an empty beanbag back across a living room carpet

lines.text: "Sit that close one more time," she warned, "and the console goes in the garage."
lines.image: {mom} alone in a living room, frowning, pointing toward the garage door

lines.text: So I asked Grandma where that rule came from, hoping to prove Mom totally wrong.
lines.image: {kid} alone sitting at a kitchen table with a notebook, determined

lines.text: Grandma said back in 1967, some brand new color TVs really did leak invisible X-rays.
lines.image: {grandma} alone in an armchair holding an old photo, an old boxy 1960s TV beside her

lines.text: Experts told every family to sit back, and that warning got passed down to Mom.
lines.image: {grandma} alone holding a faded old newspaper with no readable text, an old boxy TV far across the room

lines.text: Those leaky TVs were fixed long ago, so I was sure I'd won the argument.
lines.image: {kid} alone walking proudly down a hallway with a notebook, grinning

lines.text: I showed Mom, and she frowned, "Then why do you keep sitting so close, anyway?"
lines.image: {mom} alone in a living room, arms crossed, one eyebrow raised, curious

lines.text: I sat way back on the couch to show her, and the screen went blurry.
lines.image: {kid} alone sitting on a couch far from the TV, squinting hard, the TV screen a blur

lines.text: The doctor said sitting close never hurt my eyes; I sat close because I'm nearsighted.
lines.image: {doctor} alone in an eye clinic holding a pair of small glasses, smiling

lines.text: Now I wear glasses, game from the couch, and beat levels I used to lose.
lines.image: {kid} alone on the couch wearing new glasses, playing a video game happily, far from the TV

lines.text: Mom was wrong about the TV, right about me, and we both say we won.
lines.image: {mom} alone in a living room, smug smile, hands on hips, warm evening light
